description: alarms.v2 §2.2, §2.6, §2.8, §2.9: which slot an identity holds. Computed twice by two scripts of the text's drafter that share no code, kept out of the repository, and never blessed. `cases`: one service's instances, as its owner runs them. `bound` is its first instance's bound (256, or the cardinality its descriptor states). An identity is a letter standing for an alert key. `events`, in order, each with what the owner does (`expect`) and, but in the one case of 259 events, the records its instance then holds (`holds`: slot -> {id, state}). `raise`: the condition of an identity is found -> {put: slot, state: "firing"}; {none: "firing"} for a duplicate observation; or {refused: "bound"} where every slot below the bound holds a firing record: nothing is put, and no alarm is resolved or put over. The identity takes the slot its instance holds a record of it on, firing or resolved, else the lowest slot on which the instance holds no firing record. `resolve`: its condition cleared -> {put: slot, state: "resolved"}, the record staying on its slot, or {none: "not_firing"}. `restart`: a new instance, with the `record` its previous instance left (slot -> {id, state, reads, derives, evaluated}: whether the entry reads, whether its words derive its alert key, and whether the new instance still evaluates its rule; null for no source) and its `bound` -> for each slot of the record, in §2.9's order: `left` (at or above the new bound: neither put nor resolved), `free` (resolved, or it does not read, or its words do not derive its key: nothing is put), `resolved` (firing under a rule no longer evaluated: put resolved on its slot) or `adopted` (put again, firing, on its slot). The new instance holds what it put, and nothing else. `views`: what one reader holds of one owner, each slot's record with the `run` and `seq` of its put, its `alert_key` (null for an unnamed alarm) and its state, and the run the owner's present descriptor states -> `takes`: for each alert key, the slot the reader takes it on: the one under the present run, the later by seq of two under it, null where none is under it; and `double`: the alert keys two slots of the present run name, the break of §2.2 a tool may report. Unnamed alarms are not compared.

cases.note: W2's day: three alarms on slots 0 to 2, and a transient on 3
a duplicate observation is no act, and a resolve of what does not fire is none
a re-raise takes the slot its resolved record is still on, though a lower slot is free
a resolved slot retaken: C takes slot 0, the lowest that does not fire, over A's resolved record; A then comes back on the lowest free slot, 2
the lowest slot that does not fire is a resolved one before an empty one above it
the bound: with both slots firing the raise is refused, and nothing is put over a firing record; a resolve frees a slot at once
a resolved record takes no room: at a bound of 2, two resolved records are two free slots
256 firing alarms fill slots 0 to 255, and the 257th raise is refused

a restart mid-incident: A is adopted on its slot, B's rule is no longer evaluated and it is put resolved, R was resolved and its slot is free, P's words do not derive its key and nothing is put. A raise then takes the lowest slot on which the new instance holds no firing record: B's
a restart with no source adopts nothing: the same alarms, found again, start from slot 0
a restart under a lowered bound: slot 2 is at the new bound and is neither put nor resolved; the new instance holds two alarms and refuses a third
an entry that does not read is not adopted, as one whose words do not derive its key is not: its slot is free
an adopted alarm keeps its slot through two restarts, and resolves on it
a rule no longer evaluated at a restart: put resolved, on its slot, and its slot is then free

views.note: an owner that restarted with no record put A on slot 0, and the reader still holds its previous instance's A on slot 2: it takes the present run's
the same, the earlier instance's slot the lower one
two slots of the present run name one identity: the owner broke §2.2. The reader takes the later by seq
the later by seq is the lower slot
unnamed alarms are not compared: two slots with no alert key are two alarms
a 16-bit run and a 32-bit run of the same value are two runs
